history.period: 1799–1814 (foundation stone December 1799; completed 1814; Sanskrit slab dated Saka 1736)
history.summary: A distinctive tantric ratna temple in Bansberia: Raja Nrisinhadeb Roy Mahasay laid the foundation in December 1799 after studying kundalini and the six chakras in Varanasi (1792–1798); after his death in 1802 (second storey done), his widow Rani Sankari completed it in 1814, spending five lakh rupees (one source says one lakh — discrepancy flagged). Chunar stones and Jaipur craftsmen. The 21–27.5 m structure has 13 lotus-bud ratnas/towers; its five storeys embody 'Tantrik Satchakrabhed' — the five parts of the human body: Bajraksha, Ira, Chitrini, Pingala, Sushumna. Sanctum holds a blue-painted four-armed neem-wood idol of Hanseswari standing on a lotus from Shiva's navel (idol ~3 ft). Complex also has the terracotta Ananta Basudeba Temple (1679, Rameshwar Ray) and the Swanbhaba Kali Temple (1788); the site is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India. Deity named for Rani Hanseswari, the founder's mother. FLAGS: (1) CSV 'state' column wrongly holds 'Hooghly' — actual state is West Bengal; (2) CSV town 'Hooghly' corrected to actual town Bansberia; (3) construction cost and building height conflict across sources (5 lakh vs 1 lakh rupees; 21 m vs 27.5 m).

name: Hanseswari Temple
town_description: Bansberia is an industrial town in Hooghly district, West Bengal, between Bandel and Tribeni on the west bank of the Hooghly river; it is known for its historic Deb Roy zamindari family, the Garhbari palace, and the unique Hanseswari and Ananta Basudeba temples.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~55 km)
travel.railway: Bansberia Railway Station (10-minute walk to the temple) or Tribeni on the Howrah–Katwa/Bardhaman line
travel.road: ~50 km from Kolkata via Delhi Road (SH-6) / GT Road; local buses and autos available

visitor_information.best_time: November to February (pleasant winter and festival season); Kali Puja, Navaratri, Poush Sankranti are peak occasions
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM–12:00 PM and 4:00–8:00 PM (flag: from a secondary travel guide, not an official source)
